artists.biography: As an aside to the musical works realised by Church of the Cosmic Skull, I have decided to release some other material under my own name, via this new website, billfisher.net Rest assured that the Church has never been stronger, and will continue to spread the light of the Cosmic Rainbow with full and unstoppable force, with new songs and other tantalisations soon to follow. The works to be sent forth from this new platform will be myriad and multiform, varied in genre but of high standard and rich with heart. The first will take the form of a full studio album, an exploration into heavier realms but still very much melody driven; prog with elements of proto-metal and stoner rock. Look out for further developments soon… Yours in peace and harmony, Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Hallucinations of a Higher Truth is Bill Fisher's second solo album, released in 2021 on Septaphonic Records. The album represents a deliberate stylistic departure from his debut work, employing a stripped-down piano trio arrangement throughout. Every track features three vocal harmony lines, creating an intimate and compositionally focused listening experience that prioritizes melody and vocal interplay over the heavier instrumentation found on his previous release.

The album stands in marked contrast to Fisher's first solo effort, Mass Hypnosis and the Dark Triad, which explored prog-metal and stoner rock territories. Hallucinations of a Higher Truth instead emphasizes chamber-like arrangements and harmonic sophistication, demonstrating the artist's range across different musical contexts. The ten-track collection showcases Fisher's work as a solo artist separate from his primary project, Church of the Cosmic Skull, though both endeavors operate concurrently.

The album received mixed reception from listeners, with user ratings reflecting divided opinions on its minimalist approach. While some appreciated the compositional clarity afforded by the piano trio format, others found the stripped-down aesthetic less engaging than more densely arranged material. Despite this, the release established Fisher's solo catalog as a distinct artistic outlet, with the album available across multiple formats including physical compact discs and digital streaming platforms.
